Modified Hodrick-Prescott filter: the smoothing parameter chosen from the data

Source: R/filters.R
mhp_filter.Rd

mhp_filter() applies the modified HP filter of McDermott (1997), studied by Choudhary, Hanif and Iqbal (2014): the smoothing parameter \(\lambda\) is the one of \(1, 2, \dots,\) max_lambda that minimises a generalised cross-validation criterion, so that every series gets its own \(\lambda\) instead of the conventional 1600 or 100.

Usage

mhp_filter(
  x,
  max_lambda = 100000L,
  as_dt = TRUE,
  log_scale = FALSE,
  criterion = c("approximate", "exact")
)

# Default S3 method
mhp_filter(
  x,
  max_lambda = 100000L,
  as_dt = TRUE,
  log_scale = FALSE,
  criterion = c("approximate", "exact")
)

Arguments

x

a numeric vector or a ts object, without missing values; at least 5 observations.

max_lambda

the largest \(\lambda\) of the search over \(1, 2, \dots,\) max_lambda (default 100000).

as_dt

TRUE (default) returns a data.table; FALSE a list.

log_scale

filter the logarithm of the series (default FALSE, as in version 0.1.0).

criterion

"approximate" (default: eq. 6, as in version 0.1.0 and the published code) or "exact" (eq. 5).

Value

With as_dt = TRUE, a data.table with the columns original, trend, cycle (and time for a ts) and the attributes lambda and gcv. With as_dt = FALSE, a list of class c("mhp_mhp", "mhp", "mhp_result", "list") with original, trend, cycle, lambda, gcv as in version 0.1.0, then gcv_path (the criterion for every \(\lambda\) of the search), log_scale, criterion, trend_log and cycle_log (with log_scale = TRUE), time and frequency (for a ts). Methods: print(), plot(), ggplot2::autoplot(), mhp_interpret().

Details

For each candidate \(\lambda\) the trend \(\hat{\mathbf{g}}(\lambda)\) of hp_filter() is computed and $$\mathrm{GCV}(\lambda) = \frac{1}{T}\left(1 + \frac{2T}{\lambda}\right)\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left(x_t - \hat{g}_t(\lambda)\right)^2$$ (Choudhary et al. 2014, eq. 6; Hanif et al. 2017, eq. 4); \(\hat\lambda\) minimises it. This is Silverman's (1984) approximation of generalised cross-validation (Craven and Wahba 1979), $$\mathrm{GCV}(\lambda) = \frac{T^{-1}\sum_{t}(x_t - \hat{g}_t(\lambda))^2}{\left(1 - T^{-1}\mathrm{tr}\,\mathbf{B}(\lambda)\right)^2}$$ (Choudhary et al. 2014, eq. 5), which criterion = "exact" uses: the eigenvalues \(\mu_i\) of \(\mathbf{A}\), computed once, give \(\mathrm{tr}\,\mathbf{B}(\lambda) = \sum_i (1 + \lambda\mu_i)^{-1}\) and the residual sum of squares for every \(\lambda\) in \(O(T)\) operations (the decomposition costs \(O(T^3)\), a fraction of a second for a few hundred observations). Each trend costs \(O(T)\) operations, so the search over 100000 values takes about a second for 200 quarterly observations.

The search is that of the authors' MATLAB code (modifiedhpfilternew.m, Choudhary et al. 2014), which omits the factor \(1/T\) (it does not change the minimum) and works on the series as given; filter the logarithm of a series (as in the papers) with log_scale = TRUE or by passing log(x).

Changes from version 0.1.0. The criterion is unchanged (the help page of 0.1.0 printed the factor as \(1 + 2/(T\lambda)\), but the code used \(1 + 2T/\lambda\)); every trend is now a banded solve instead of a dense one, so results agree with 0.1.0 to rounding error at a fraction of the time.

References

Choudhary, M. A., Hanif, M. N. and Iqbal, J. (2014). On smoothing macroeconomic time series using the modified HP filter. Applied Economics, 46(19), 2205–2214. doi:10.1080/00036846.2014.894631

Craven, P. and Wahba, G. (1979). Smoothing noisy data with spline functions. Numerische Mathematik, 31, 377–403. doi:10.1007/BF01404567

Silverman, B. W. (1984). A fast and efficient cross-validation method for smoothing parameter choice in spline regression. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 79(387), 584–589. doi:10.1080/01621459.1984.10478084

McDermott, C. J. (1997). An automatic method for choosing the smoothing parameter in the HP filter. Unpublished, International Monetary Fund, Washington DC; described in Coe, D. T. and McDermott, C. J. (1997). Does the gap model work in Asia? IMF Staff Papers, 44(1), 59–80. doi:10.2307/3867497

See also

hp_filter, fmhp_filter, mhp_batch, get_lambda

Examples

data(us_macro)
gdp <- ts(data = us_macro$gdp, start = c(1959, 1), frequency = 4)
mhp <-
  mhp_filter(
      x          = log(gdp)
    , max_lambda = 100000
    , as_dt      = FALSE
    , log_scale  = FALSE
    , criterion  = "approximate"
    )
mhp
#> Modified HP Filter Result
#> ==============================
#> Observations: 203 
#> Optimal lambda: 683 
#> GCV: 2.82e-04 
#> 
#> Cycle Statistics:
#>   Mean: -1.634e-13 
#>   SD:   0.01333 
#>   AR1:  0.828 
#>   Range: 0.07802 
#> 
#> Sources: Hodrick and Prescott (1997); McDermott (1997); Coe and McDermott
#> (1997); Choudhary et al. (2014); Choudhary et al. (2014, MATLAB code). Full
#> references: mhp_cite(x).
plot(x = mhp)
